etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Latin sēparātus, perfect passive participle of sēparāre (“to separate”), from sē (“apart”) +‎ parō (“prepare”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *per- (“produce, procure, bring forward, bring forth”). Displaced Middle English scheden, from Old English scēadan (whence English shed).

definitions.definition: Apart from (the rest); not connected to or attached to (anything else).
(transitive) To divide (a thing) into separate parts.
(transitive) To disunite from a group or mass; to disconnect.

quote.citation: 1683, John Dryden, The Art of Poetry:
quote.text: From the fine gold I separate the allay [alloy].

quote.citation: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London:  […]  Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, Romans 8:35:
quote.text: Who shall separate us from the love of Christ?

definitions.definition: (transitive) To cause (things or people) to be separate.

quote.citation: 2013 June 7, David Simpson, “Fantasy of navigation”, in The Guardian Weekly, volume 188, number 26, page 36:
quote.text: It is tempting to speculate about the incentives or compulsions that might explain why anyone would take to the skies in [the] basket [of a balloon]: […];  […]; or perhaps to muse on the irrelevance of the borders that separate nation states and keep people from understanding their shared environment.

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To divide itself into separate pieces or substances.
(obsolete) To set apart; to select from among others, as for a special use or service.

quote.citation: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London:  […]  Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, Acts 13:2:
quote.text: Separate me Barnabas and Saul for the work whereunto I have called them.

definitions.definition: (usually in the plural) Anything that is sold by itself, especially articles of clothing such as blouses, skirts, jackets, and pants.

quote.citation: 2017 October 2, Jess Cartner-Morle, “Stella McCartney lays waste to disposable fashion in Paris”, in the Guardian‎[1]:
quote.text: French taffeta evening separates – a puffball skirt, and a ruffled blouse – were pressed flat to drag them up to date.

definitions.definition: (bibliography) A printing of an article from a periodical as its own distinct publication and distributed independently, often with different page numbers.
